questions.questionTextEn: In India, there is only one Constitution for the Centre as well as for each state. However, a state is exception to it. That state is
questions.questionTextHi: भारत में केंद्र के साथ-साथ प्रत्येक राज्य के लिए एक ही संविधान है। हालाँकि, एक राज्य इसका अपवाद है। वह अवस्था है
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). There was one Constitution for all the Indian States and the Centre, but the State of Jammu and Kashmir was an exception to this, because there were certain temporary provisions with respect to the State of Jammu and Kashmir under Article 370. This State had its separate Constitution. Article 370 was declared inoperative on 6 August 2019 by a Presidential order. Now Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh are two separate Union territories of Indian Union.

Now Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh are two separate Union territories of Indian Union.

questions.questionTextEn: Providing special status to the state of Jammu and Kashmir under the Indian constitution means -
questions.questionTextHi: भारतीय संविधान के अंतर्गत जम्मू एवं कश्मीर राज्य को विशेष दर्जा प्रदान करने का अर्थ है -
optionsEn: Parliament does not have the right to legislate.
Only the President can make Acts.
Only Legislative Assembly has the right to legislate.
optionsHi: संसद को कानून बनाने का अधिकार नहीं है.
केवल राष्ट्रपति ही अधिनियम बना सकता है।
कानून बनाने का अधिकार केवल विधान सभा को है।
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). There were certain temporary provisions with respect to the State of Jammu and Kashmir enshrined under Article 370. It had its own separate Constitution. Administration and provisions of this State were diﬀ erent from other States. The State of Jammu and Kashmir was not included in the deﬁ nition of the States provided in Article 152 of Chapter 1 of Part VI of the Constitution. On August 9, 2019, by a Presidential order, Jammu and Kashmir became a Union Territory.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (A) There were certain temporary provisions with respect to the State of Jammu and Kashmir enshrined under Article 370. It had its own separate Constitution. questions.questionTextEn: Articles of the Constitution of India that apply on their own to the State of Jammu and Kashmir, are
questions.questionTextHi: भारत के संविधान के अनुच्छेद जो जम्मू और कश्मीर राज्य पर स्वयं लागू होते हैं
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). During the question period, Article 1 and Article 370 of the Indian Constitution were automatically imposed in the state of Jammu and Kashmir. Article 1, where the state of Jammu and Kashmir declared as an integral part of Indian territory, on the other hand Article 370, gave special status to Jammu and Kashmir. Currently, no special status has been granted to Jammu and Kashmir. The state of Jammu and Kashmir does not exist at present. In its place, two union territories namely Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh exist.

questions.questionTextEn: When was the designation Sadr-e-Riyasat changed to Governor for the state of Jammu and Kashmir? (a) 1948 (b) 1950 (c) 1952 (c) 1967 U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1997
questions.questionTextHi: जम्मू-कश्मीर राज्य के लिए सदर-ए-रियासत का पदनाम बदलकर राज्यपाल कब किया गया? (ए) 1948 (बी) 1950 (सी) 1952 (सी) 1967 यू.पी.पी.सी.एस. (पूर्व) 1997
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). The Constituent Assembly of Jammu and Kashmir abolished the hereditary rule of Maharaja and elected Karn Singh as the First Sadr-e-Riyasat of Jammu and Kashmir in 1951. Later, the name ‘Sadr-e-Riyasat’ was renamed as ‘Governor’ by Sixth Amendment Act, 1965 of the Constitution of Jammu and Kashmir. Thus, none of the given option (answer) is correct. Election Commission *Article 324 to 329 in part XV of the Constitution deals with the provisions related to the electoral system. *According to article 324 there shall be an election commission which is a permanent and independent body. *This commission is responsible for superintendence, direction and control of conducting the elections to the parliament, State Assemblies, the President and the Vice-President. *The election commission is consist of a Chief Election Commissioner and other election commissioners (the number being decided by the President time to time) [art. 324(2)]. The Chief Election Commissioner and other election commissioners are appointed by the president. *Till 15 October, 1989 there was only one election commissioner but on 16 October, 1989 two more additional election commissioners were appointed for the ﬁ rst time. *But these posts were in eﬀ ect upto the 1st of January 1990. *On 1st October 1993, again two additional election commissioners were appointed and since then the election commission has three member. At present there are three Election Commissioners in the Election Commission. They have equal power and their salary and perks are same as that of the Judges of the supreme court. *Their tenure is of 6 year or up to the age of 65 years (whichever is earlier). *The chief election commissioner can be removed from his oﬃ ce only in a manner and on the ground prescribed for removal of Judges of the supreme court [Article 324(5)]. *Other Election Commissioner or the state election commissioner can be removed by the President on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner. *The notiﬁ cation for the election to the Lok sabha and Rajya sabha is issued by the President and for the state legislative assemblies by the Governor. *Article 326 mentions the provision of Adult Suﬀ rage. Right to vote in India is statutory Right. *As per the people representation act 1951, there is right to vote and being elected in India. *The age for right to vote was decreased from 21 years to 18 years by the 61st Constitutional Amendment act 1988 which come into eﬀ ect from 28 march 1989. *The election to local bodies (Panchayats and municipalities) is being conducted by the State Election Commission. *The Delimitation commission is a commission established by Government of India. Its main task is to redraw the boundaries of various assemblies and lok sabha constituencies based on the recent census. Till now, Delimitation commission has been set up for ﬁ ve times (1952, 1963, 1973, 2002 and 2020). Note : Fifth Delimitation commission constituted in March 2020.
